title: Stop kbs dirtying tracked files on ordinary use
description:
Problem: ordinary kbs use dirties the working tree. It regenerates right_now_summary / right_now_updated_at on issue files and appends to project/events/llm_usage.jsonl (1,400+ lines appended locally in the Papyrus checkout). This causes aborted git pulls and 11 merge conflicts on summary / updated_at / closed_at fields.

Evidence: reported 2026-10-12/13 in Papyrus. Source confirms the writers exist: rust/src/right_now.rs, rust/src/summarize.rs and rust/src/lifecycle_compaction.rs reference right_now_summary; llm_usage is referenced in rust/src/summarize.rs. Not reproduced: whether a pure read command (list/show) writes files; needs a test.

Acceptance:
- Read commands (list, show, now, ready, validate) never modify tracked files (checked by git status clean after each in a Gherkin scenario).
- Generated or derived data (right-now summaries, LLM usage log) lives outside tracked files (for example the overlay cache or an untracked/ignored path) or is in a merge-friendly form (per-writer append-only files, no shared mutable fields).
- Existing boards migrate without conflicts.

Reproduced 2026-10-13 with kbs 0.32.0 in a clean clone: a single kbs create modified the tracked file project/events/llm_usage.jsonl (appended a line) and was the only tracked change beyond the new issue file. Plain kbs list and kbs validate left git status clean, so the read-only claim is narrower than reported (the right-now summary generation on show/create is the remaining suspect).
right_now_summary: A clean-clone test confirmed `kbs create` changes tracked files, while `list` and `validate` leave them clean.
